_about: Documented, reviewed exceptions for the differential gate (differential.py). Each entry silences ONE (target, check) deviation because the independent target is KNOWN to legitimately deviate on that point — e.g. a real, reported bug in that target, or a capability the target implements to an older pinned version. An entry needs the target name, the check id, and a substantive reason (with a link/citation where possible). This exists so a genuine target bug can never silently mask one of OUR check bugs: every deviation is either resolved (fix the check or the target) or explained here. An empty allow list is the healthy default — it means every check agrees with every independent conformant target we test. SELF-EXPIRY (differential.py classify_allowlist, mirroring known_reference_defects.json / known_fuzz_defects.json): each entry is an ACTIVE claim that its (target, check) deviation STILL occurs. If we PROBE the entry's target this run but its silenced deviation NO LONGER occurs (upstream fixed the bug, or our check changed), the entry is STALE and the differential gate FAILS naming it to delete — so a documented silence can never outlive its deviation and thereby mask a FUTURE, different regression of the same (target, check). An entry whose target is not probed this run is untestable and left alone.
_expiry_log: 2026-08-13: BOTH remaining entries (nodejs-reference-sample checkout.protocol_error_shape CHK-050 + checkout.unavailable_all_error_envelope CHK-053, the flat-detail error-shape class) self-expired RED on the samples re-pin 52377503->ab78116 and were DELETED per the contract above — our samples#174 (merged 2026-08-12) converted all 18 flat-detail sites to the UCP error envelope, so the Node reference no longer deviates. This is the designed payoff loop: file the fix upstream, re-pin, let the silence expire. Full entry text lives in git history at this file. Earlier expiries: DISC-003/PAY-003 entries (samples#168) removed at the 2026-08-11 re-pin.

allow.reason: Reported upstream as samples#191: the python reference returns HTTP 500 for any checkout create carrying attribution, because checkout_service.py:406 calls model_dump on a value that ucp-sdk 0.4.4 types as a TypeAliasType and therefore leaves as a plain dict. overview.md requires that the presence or absence of attribution MUST NOT affect the response, so this is a target defect and not a false flag from our check. https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/samples/issues/191

Reported upstream as samples#188: the python reference returns HTTP 500 for a cart create carrying currency, because cart_service.py:113 dumps the request excluding only line_items and then passes currency explicitly at :119, so the request supplied member collides with the keyword argument and raises TypeError. cart.json marks currency ucp_request omit, so a conformant probe may send it and the merchant still owns the value. The probe body is well formed, so this is a target defect and not a fixture-specific misreading by our check. https://github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/samples/issues/188
